did_you_know.text: Did you know? On the day the construction of the Tabernacle was completed, Moses anointed and consecrated the Tabernacle, all its furnishings, the altar, and its furnishings. In this way, both the structure and its equipment were dedicated to sacred service.
Did you know? The leaders of Israel brought a total of six carts and twelve oxen: one cart for every two leaders and one ox for each leader.
Did you know? The Lord commanded that the carts and oxen be used for the work of the Tent of Meeting and distributed among the Levites according to their duties.
Did you know? The Gershonites received two carts and four oxen, in keeping with their responsibility to carry the parts of the Tabernacle assigned to them.
Did you know? The Merarites received four carts and eight oxen because their duties included carrying the heavier parts of the Tabernacle.
Did you know? The Kohathites did not receive any carts or oxen because they carried their sacred objects on their shoulders.
Did you know? The dedication of the altar lasted twelve days, with one of the leaders of Israel presenting an offering each day.
Did you know? Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of the tribe of Judah, was the first to present his offering for the dedication of the altar.

Did you know? Each leader’s offering included silver vessels filled with flour mixed with oil, a gold ladle filled with incense, and animals for burnt offerings, sin offerings, and fellowship offerings.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it is described how Moses heard the voice of the Lord speaking to him from above the cover of the Ark of the Covenant, from between the two cherubim.
